# WO-261104-4E17A · Exhaust fan F-201

**Priority:** P1 (within 24 h)  
**Failure mode:** VIB – Vibration (ISO 14224)  
**Suspected cause:** Forcing frequency coincident with a structural natural frequency (posterior 0.73)  
**Raised by:** muse-wonder-1.0 · 2026-11-04 10:09

Leading fault: resonance P=0.733, 1× critical 363 rpm (mode 6.055±0.063 Hz, ζ=0.030±0.012; FDD 6.094 Hz, shroud/frame phase -100.8°). Program/verify skip bands 163–200 and 327–400 rpm, avoid dwell, and capture steady-speed triaxial phase above the critical to make imbalance/misalignment evaluable. Amplitudes are uncalibrated (relative only) — do not use 602/421 mm/s RMS for ISO severity.

## Evidence
- critical speed inside the swept range (Q) = 27.9 (+13.0 dB)
- Amplitudes uncalibrated: severity from frequencies and ratios
- Running speed 408 rpm (audio (blade pass) · kinematic posterior (×0.285))

## Safety
- Lock out / tag out (LOTO) the drive and isolate process energy
- Guards back on before restart; no loose clothing near rotating parts

## Tasks
1. Program VFD skip frequencies over the resonance bands (Argonaut can do this).
2. If the duty needs that speed: detune the structure. To move fn above the forcing by 15 %, stiffness must rise by the factor computed below (mass unchanged). Here: fn = 6.05 Hz, 1x = 6.81 Hz -> stiffness x1.67 (fn ∝ √k).
3. Re-run a coast-down; confirm the Campbell crossing has moved out of the operating range.

## Parts
- Bracing / stiffener per detuning calculation

**Estimated time:** 1.0 h

## Verification
Re-measure with Argonaut after the work; acceptance: fault posterior < 0.2 and ISO zone A/B (or unchanged frequencies/ratios if uncalibrated).

text:
## Exhaust fan F-201 — assessment complete

**Speed / kinematics (confident)**
- Bayesian speed posterior: MAP **412.9 rpm**, p_map = 0.97, 68% CI 412.3–413.6 rpm, 15/18 peaks explained; order-tracked speed now **408.4 rpm (6.81 Hz)** — consistent with the audio-documented run-up (starts ~00:04, continuously accelerating, no steady state reached). The ½× alternative carries only p = 0.028, so no kinematic re-test was needed. No display rpm was available as an independent check.
- Machine model: 6-blade axial fan, 50 Hz line, blade-pass excitation in audio.

**Primary finding — resonance (WARN, P = 0.73)**
- Structural mode at **6.055 ± 0.063 Hz, ζ = 0.030 ± 0.012** (order-tracked SDOF fit), corroborated by an FDD mode at 6.094 Hz, ζ = 0.023, shroud/frame phase ≈ −101°.
- Campbell diagram: **1× critical at 363 rpm**, inside the operating sweep. Current 408 rpm is only ~12% above the critical and just 2% above the optimiser's upper exclusion edge — an unacceptably thin margin. Evidence: critical in swept range, Q = 27.9 (+13.0 dB).
- Secondary FDD modes at 2.81, 7.73 and 10.55 Hz noted; the 2.81 Hz mode is heavily damped (ζ = 0.165).

**Amplitude caveat — no ISO severity claim**
- `scale_calibrated = false` (reported 602/421 mm/s RMS are physically implausible for this machine). All conclusions rest on frequencies, orders, phase and ratios only. Relative order amplitudes now: 1× = 5.71, 2× = 2.75 (ratio 0.48), 3× ≈ 0.

**Other hypotheses**
- Blade-pass/flow excitation: P = 0.44 but with a wide range (0.03–0.45) — inconclusive on transient data; needs a steady-speed capture.
- Looseness: P = 0.004 — effectively ruled out (harmonics −8.7 dB, half-orders −4.3 dB).
- Imbalance and misalignment: **not evaluable** (posterior = prior, no phase/coupling data in a run-up transient). A constant-speed triaxial capture with phase across the coupling is required before either can be confirmed — so no balancing was proposed (imbalance P = 0.15 < 0.5 threshold).
- Cavitation: index 0.0019, no HF impulsive signature, and the asset is a fan — not applicable.

## Optimisation — no feasible setpoint
The optimiser (duty ≥ 80% of current, 10% resonance margin) returned **infeasible**: no speed satisfies duty, resonance and severity constraints together. Exclusion bands: **163–200 rpm** and **327–400 rpm**. Proposing a lower setpoint would either breach the duty floor or park the fan inside the 363 rpm critical band, so **no setpoint change was submitted** and no energy/CO₂ saving is claimed. Options for the operator: accept duty < 80% to run below the critical, or detune the structure — the work order calculates a **stiffness increase ×1.67** to lift fₙ 15% above the 1× forcing. NPSH is not applicable (fan).

## Actions queued
1. **Skip bands (a093cc)** — program VFD skip frequencies over 163–200 and 327–400 rpm; no drive is connected, so this is written into the work order as a technician step: traverse the critical promptly, never dwell at 327–400 rpm.
2. **Work order WO-261104-4E17A (P1, 24 h)** — resonance at 363 rpm: program/verify skip bands, assess stiffening (×1.67 per detuning calc), then a verification coast-down to confirm the Campbell crossing has moved clear. Uncalibrated amplitudes are flagged in the WO so no one acts on the 602/421 mm/s figures.
3. **Follow-up re-measurement due 2026-11-11** — steady-speed triaxial capture above the critical with phase across the coupling (to make imbalance/misalignment evaluable), a calibrated scale reference, and confirmation that fault posterior drops below 0.2.

**Bottom line:** hold current speed, stay out of 327–400 rpm except in transit, and complete WO-261104-4E17A before considering any duty reduction or detuning decision.
